newsitem.title: USA: Governor's Miami order protects bondholders.
newsitem.headline: Governor's Miami order protects bondholders.

text.p: The executive order that Florida's governor issued when he appointed the Miami oversight board contains an important provision for bondholders -- it requires that debt service revenues be held by a trustee.

Gov. Lawton Chiles signed the 11-page order late Wednesday. It specifies that "pledged revenues for principal and interest payments of outstanding debt shall be placed with a third party trustee to ensure that all debt obligations of the city will be met."
It also specifies that the trustee agreement must be approved by the oversight board, and that the trustee shall deduct the money from monthly revenues before releasing any money to the city.

City finance officials were not immediately available for comment on that provision on Thursday, but they have acknowledged in the past that bond proceeds and revenues pledged to debt service were often co-mingled with other revenues.

The order also specifies how long Miami will remain under state oversight. Once the city has produced two years or balanced budgets, the board will continue to to oversee its budgets for three more years.
The five-member board, led by Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay, was assigned to assist Miami in drafting a new budget and report back to the governor, but has not authority to override the city commission.
